title: Implications of Annotation Artifacts in Edge Probing Test Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: The paper analyzes standard edge probing datasets for superficial cues or 'artifacts' that allow models to solve tasks using simple heuristics rather than linguistic knowledge. Specifically, it measures the prevalence of exact string memorization (Mem-Exact) and label frequency (Mem-Freq) heuristics and evaluates model performance on filtered datasets where these artifacts are removed.

The authors quantify 'repetition bias' by calculating the percentage of test data points that are present in the training data with the same label, allowing classifiers to succeed via exact string matching (the Mem-Exact heuristic).
